qa.question: How do the cork and clay demos keep moisture away from the jar?
required_facts: The cork lid absorbs moisture near the rim.
The clay lid has a groove that channels drops away.

ask.answer: Cork absorbs moisture while the clay groove channels drops away.

collection.overview: Two demos use different lids to keep a jar dry.

themes.title: Lid moisture control
themes.summary: The two lids redirect moisture in different ways.

perspectives.statement: Cork absorbs water near the rim.
The clay lid uses a groove to redirect drops.

evidence_catalog.text: The cork at the rim drinks in the stray drops.
Drops go out through a groove under the clay lid.
We press wax dots next to the handle.
